calls.reason: PHRBench and MDH-Bench document reliability failures, while Epoch records verified mathematical successes. These mixed results do not clearly establish the broad imbalance across prediction, reasoning, facts and instructions.
DeepMind's AlphaFold release assessment and the study of biological screening failures address narrow uses. They do not establish how much current AI poses little danger in ordinary use.

AAAI documents convergence toward neural approaches, while Google reports continuing world-model work. Neither establishes convergence specifically on LLMs or their prediction superiority; the puzzle study addresses only narrower weaknesses.
This is an interpretive opinion about the controversy. Butlin and Chandaria offer theory-based consciousness arguments, but neither study establishes what drives the wider debate.

The Fenix court order records hallucinated authorities and additions despite instructions restricting outside sources. Xu's copyright experiment finds copying persists despite explicit warnings. Together they support the ordinary claim that prohibitions can fail.

Rocchetti finds varied instruction-following mechanisms; Fu finds both spurious correlations and improved causal patterns after training. Neither establishes that reliance on correlations explains the instruction failures Marcus describes.
